AN ACT to amend the social services law, in relation to requiring statewide
training for child protective services workers to include how to identify an
abused or maltreated child with an intellectual or developmental disability
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6463

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the social services law, in relation to requiring state-
wide training for child protective services workers to include how to
identify an abused or maltreated child with an intellectual or develop-
mental disability

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to require the office of children and family
services to provide child protective services employees with training to
identify an abused or maltreated child when such child is an individual
with an intellectual or developmental disability.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend section 421 of the Social Services
Law by requiring the office of children and family services to provide
training to child protective services employees, included in the ongoing
statewide training program, for identifying an abused or maltreated
child when such child is an individual with an intellectual or develop-
mental disability.

Section 2 of this bill provides that the effective date shall take
effect one year from when this act shall have become law, provided,
however, that effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or
repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of
this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and completed
on or before such effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In May 2021, a 17-year-old boy with cerebral palsy died of sepsis and
malnutrition in Oswego County, when he passed he was only 55 pounds.
Child Protective Services (CPS) failed to adequately address the situ-
ation despite repeated attempts at contact from family members, thera-
pists, and aides. In March 2022, the couple was arrested and charged for
abuse and neglect of their child.

Cases like this are abject tragedies that can be prevented with a proper
network of support. In 2021, 56,760 children experienced abuse or
maltreatment, including cases of neglect and emotional, physical, or
sexual abuse, in the State. Many of these cases involve children that
have an intellectual or developmental disability, who often require
unique support from their families, the community, and the State.

Providing training focused on individuals with an intellectual or devel-
opmental disability would improve the responsiveness of CPS workers to
cases that involve such children. This would enhance outcomes for child
abuse cases that involve children with an intellectual or developmental
disability, protecting the well-being and lives of numerous children
across the State.This bill would require the Office of Children and
Family Services to provide training to child protective services employ-
ees, included in the ongoing statewide training program, for identifying
an abused or maltreated child when such child is an individual with an
intellectual or developmental disability.
 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect one year from when this act shall have become
law, provided, however, that effective immediately, the addition, amend-
ment and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implemen-
tation of this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and
completed on or before such effective date.

BILL NUMBER: S6463A

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the social services law, in relation to updating the
mandated reporter training to include how to identify an abused or
maltreated child with an intellectual or developmental disability

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to require the Office of Children and Family
Services (OCFS) to update the mandated reporter training to include the
identification of an abused or maltreated child with an intellectual or
developmental disability.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend section 413 of the Social Services
Law by requiring OCFS to update the training issued to mandated repor-
ters to include the identification of an abused or maltreated child with
an intellectual or developmental disability.

Section 2 of this bill would amend section 421 of the Social Services
Law to require OCFS to update training issued to local child protective
services to include guidance on how to identify an abused or maltreated
child with an intellectual or developmental disability.

Section 3 of this bill provides that the effective date shall take
effect one year from when it shall have become a law. Effective imme-
diately, the addition, amendment and/or repeal of any rule or regulation
necessary for the implementation of this act on its effective date are
authorized to be made and completed on or before such effective date.
